patch_description: Replace the causal weighted moving average (which introduces lag and phase delay) with a hybrid zero-phase filter: (1) a 1st-order adaptive Kalman filter whose measurement noise R is estimated online from local residual variance, giving strong noise reduction with responsiveness; (2) a short Savitzky-Golay smoothing pass that preserves polynomial trends (slope) without lag (centered window); (3) an optional endpoint extension (reflect-padding) so output length matches input length, drastically reducing lag error since no samples are dropped. The Kalman gain adapts: high local noise → more smoothing (fewer false reversals/slope changes); low noise → responsive tracking. Savgol preserves slopes (trend dynamics), reducing slope changes and false reversals while keeping tracking accuracy. All operations are O(N), keeping efficiency high.
